name: Czech Technical University in Prague
summary: Prague technical university: 11 English bachelor's in seven faculties and an institute, from civil engineering to quantum physics and flying.

ib.text: CTU says IB Diploma holders skip its assessment and nostrification: send certified copies straight to the faculty. Each faculty sets its own test or interview; none asks for IB points.

apply.via: CTU e-application (one per faculty, CZK 950 each)

programmes.name: Civil Engineering
programmes.about: Four years of structural and building engineering: two years of science and core courses, then design projects and electives in concrete, steel, timber and masonry structures, building materials and building services, ending in a bachelor project.
programmes.overview: The four years start with fundamental sciences and basic professional courses, then move to specialised courses and design projects in which you choose electives to match your interests. Content centres on structural design, load-bearing and non-load-bearing structures, building services and construction technology. A three-week internship at a civil engineering company adds practice, and the degree closes with a bachelor's thesis. Graduates work as structural designers in concrete, steel, timber or masonry, or as construction managers, and can continue to master's programmes in English or Czech.
programmes.ib: Written maths test in Prague, which cannot be waived. English: your school-leaving exam in English, a B2 certificate, or proof your school taught in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on a 70-minute, 15-question maths test (no calculator); you need at least 8 of 20 points. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

lastYear.text: 31 March; maths test in early June

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.about: Broad mechanical engineering with no fixed specialisation: maths, physics and design first, then fluid dynamics, mechanics, strength of materials, machine elements and energy conversion, with elective blocks in transport, technology or energy.
programmes.overview: Across six semesters you study mathematics, physics, mechanics, strength of materials, thermomechanics and fluid dynamics, together with materials science, casting, forming, welding and machining, electrical circuits, machine elements, automatic control and digital design. Lectures are balanced with tutorials and laboratory work, and the last year centres on projects and the bachelor thesis. There are no formal specialisations; groups of elective courses in transport, technology and energy let you point your thesis in a direction. Graduates are prepared for any engineering master's or technical roles in industry.
programmes.ib: Scio online test "Mathematics in English" at the 50th percentile or better. Recommended English level B2 (IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 65).
programmes.selectionNote: Sit Scio's online Mathematics in English test early in the year and reach the 50th percentile; the faculty then checks your documents. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

lastYear.text: Scio test by 1 March; documents by 30 June

programmes.name: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
programmes.about: One programme joining electrical engineering and computer science, with three branches you can mix freely across: compulsory core courses plus electives, aimed at a master's in Prague or abroad.
programmes.overview: This English-taught degree joins electrical engineering and computer science in one programme, combining theory with practical training and cross-disciplinary elements. Instead of formal specialisations, three branches let you shape your emphasis, and you can freely combine compulsory elective courses across them. The aim is graduates who understand both the hardware and software sides of modern technology. It prepares you for master's studies in the Czech Republic or abroad.
programmes.ib: English certificate unless you are a native speaker: TOEFL iBT 70, IELTS 6 or TOEIC 800; Duolingo is not accepted.
programmes.selectionNote: Send your transcript, motivation letter and English certificate; then an online interview, sometimes with a test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Mathematical Engineering
programmes.about: Classical and modern mathematics with physics and informatics, applied to science and engineering, with specialisations in mathematical physics, mathematical informatics or mathematical modelling.
programmes.overview: You build a base in mathematical analysis, functional analysis and numerical mathematics alongside physics and computer science, and learn to turn mathematics into working applications on modern computers. Three tracks let you specialise: mathematical modelling of biological, environmental and materials phenomena, mathematical physics with links to quantum technologies, or mathematical informatics, covering programming, networks, GPU computing, image analysis and neural networks. Graduates go into research, IT and industry as software developers or data analysts, or continue to the follow-up master's.
programmes.ib: B2 English certificate required: Cambridge B2 (e.g. FCE), IELTS 5.5, TOEFL at B2 or TELC B2.
programmes.selectionNote: No entrance exam in 2026: the Dean waived it, so applicants with a school-leaving qualification and B2 English were admitted. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Nuclear and Particle Physics
programmes.about: Nuclear, particle and quantum physics with maths, experimental methods and programming; some teaching runs with research partners such as the Czech Academy of Sciences and CERN.
programmes.overview: The core subjects are quantum mechanics, subatomic physics, waves, optics and atomic physics, supported by mathematics, experimental methods and programming. Teaching takes place on campus and through partnerships with the Czech Academy of Sciences and CERN, which bring research experience into the course. You learn measurement techniques and data analysis, including machine learning. Graduates head into scientific research, accelerator and nuclear facilities, environmental and medical applications or industry, and can continue to the follow-up master's in the same field.
programmes.ib: B2 English certificate required: Cambridge B2 (e.g. FCE), IELTS 5.5, TOEFL at B2 or TELC B2.
programmes.selectionNote: No entrance exam in 2026: the Dean waived it, so applicants with a school-leaving qualification and B2 English were admitted. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Physical Engineering
programmes.about: Physics combined with maths and computing through theory, labs and computer work, with specialisations from plasma physics and fusion to solid state, lasers and photonics, and computer physics.
programmes.overview: Physics is combined with mathematics and computer science, covering mechanics, electricity and magnetism, optics and theoretical physics. Laboratory courses include laser technique, electron microscopy and the structure of solids, and you work with computer algebra systems and study plasma physics. Five specialisations are on offer: plasma physics and thermonuclear fusion, physical engineering of materials, solid state engineering, laser technology and photonics, and computer physics. Graduates work in research laboratories and technology development in fields such as semiconductors, photonics, automotive and telecommunications.
programmes.ib: B2 English certificate required: Cambridge B2 (e.g. FCE), IELTS 5.5, TOEFL at B2 or TELC B2.
programmes.selectionNote: No entrance exam in 2026: the Dean waived it, so applicants with a school-leaving qualification and B2 English were admitted. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Quantum Technologies
programmes.about: Quantum mechanics, solid-state physics and laser technology with maths and informatics, plenty of lab work and two foreign-language courses, preparing for quantum, nanomaterial and secure-communication work.
programmes.overview: This multidisciplinary degree balances physics, mathematics and informatics, with teaching in quantum mechanics, solid state physics, laser technology, waves, optics and atomic physics. A quantum laboratory and work with modern computing give you hands-on experience, and foreign-language classes and cooperation with foreign projects prepare you for international teamwork. Graduates move into scientific research and technical companies, for example in nanomaterials, laser technologies and secure communications, or continue to the follow-up master's in Quantum Technologies.
programmes.ib: B2 English certificate required: Cambridge B2 (e.g. FCE), IELTS 5.5, TOEFL at B2 or TELC B2.
programmes.selectionNote: No entrance exam in 2026: the Dean waived it, so applicants with a school-leaving qualification and B2 English were admitted. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Professional Pilot
programmes.about: A university degree with integrated ATPL(A) airline-pilot training: theory at the faculty, flying at a partner flight school you choose in your first month, leading to an EASA licence valid across Europe.
programmes.overview: The degree pairs university coursework in aviation operations, safety and aircraft management with integrated ATPL(A) flight training, which is the practical core of the studies. Flight training takes place at partner flight schools, and you choose your school early in the first year. Graduates qualify to fly as pilot in command or co-pilot on multi-crew commercial aircraft, to act as pilot in command in aerial work, or to take management roles in civil aviation, with qualifications valid across the EASA member states.
programmes.ib: You need a Class 1 medical before flight training and pay the flight school yourself, about CZK 1,650,000. B2 English, or proof of earlier study in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Written maths and English tests in Prague in June, 20 points each: you need 20 of 40, with at least 7 in each; ranked on points. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Biomedical Technology
programmes.about: Training as a biomedical technician: maths, physics and chemistry with anatomy and physiology, then medical devices, imaging systems, hospital IT and healthcare technology management; an accredited health profession for work in hospitals.
programmes.overview: Taught in English, the degree pairs mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology with medical content: biomechanics, imaging systems, healthcare information systems, clinical laboratory instruments and anaesthesiology equipment, plus healthcare legislation, economics and management. Theory is balanced with practice in how medical technology works and is used. Graduates are prepared to maintain and inspect devices, assess failures, help procure equipment and train staff in hospitals, or to work in research, manufacturing, certification and servicing of medical equipment.
programmes.ib: Medical fitness certificate on the faculty form. B2 English certificate, unless your school taught in English or you take the Teams interview.
programmes.selectionNote: Admitted on your English motivation letter; a Teams interview in English replaces a missing B2 certificate. Up to 40 places. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Informatics
programmes.about: One computing programme in which you choose a specialisation during your studies: computer engineering, information security, software engineering, networks and internet, computer science, or computer systems and virtualisation.
programmes.overview: The programme combines theory of how computers work and a solid dose of mathematics with many practical exercises and work on real projects with companies. You pick one of six specialisations along the way: information security, computer engineering, computer networks and the internet, computer systems and virtualization, software engineering, or computer science. Internships and research projects link you to industry, and the training suits both employment in the IT sector and continuing in academic study.
programmes.ib: B2 English: a certificate such as IELTS 5.5 or TOEFL iBT 65, or a document showing your school taught in English.
programmes.selectionNote: FIT's maths test in Prague (50 of 100 minimum) or a Scio online test, Maths in English or GAP (60th percentile); ranked on the result. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

lastYear.text: 31 March; maths test or Scio by 12 May

programmes.name: Economics and Management
programmes.about: Economics, business and management at CTU's Masaryk Institute of Advanced Studies, with technical electives for modern industry and a three-month company internship in the fifth semester.
programmes.overview: Compulsory courses cover mathematics, business economics, informatics, accounting principles, logistics, human resource management and principles of management. Classes are small, and you add elective technical courses on modern industry and social and communication courses that build soft skills for multicultural workplaces. A three-month internship at an established company comes in the fifth semester, and short study stays in Europe and overseas are possible. Graduates enter roles in finance, marketing, sales, HR, operations and public administration, or continue to a master's in innovation project management.
programmes.ib: Your English is tested in the entrance exam, so no certificate is needed.
programmes.selectionNote: Online maths and English test (35 points) and a 15-minute interview (10 points); pass with 27 of 45 and each part's minimum. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: Each faculty, and the Masaryk Institute, runs its own application, CZK 950 fee, deadline and test: two faculties means two applications.
Some faculty pages still ask for nostrification of foreign diplomas; Czech law now accepts the IB Diploma without it, and CTU's own IB page says so: point the faculty to that page.
English-taught study is charged to EU citizens too: CZK 55,000 a semester at most faculties, CZK 64,000 at Information Technology.
